summary.oneLiner: Shanti Spintex delivered record H1FY26 revenue of ₹382cr driven by capacity utilization of 89.9% and Teesta Spintex acquisition, but PAT declined due to pricing pressure; the path to margin expansion now hinges on backward integration into dyeing (commissioning Dec’26/Jan’27) and renewable energy capex, which together are expected to lift PAT to ₹30cr by FY28.

one-line thesis: Shanti Spintex delivered record H1FY26 revenue of ₹382cr driven by capacity utilization of 89.9% and Teesta Spintex acquisition, but PAT declined due to pricing pressure; the path to margin expansion now hinges on backward integration into dyeing (commissioning Dec’26/Jan’27) and renewable energy capex, which together are expected to lift PAT to ₹30cr by FY28.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +8% YoY (₹382cr H1FY26); EBITDA: ₹10cr, margin 2.6% (down from prior); PAT (reported): ₹7cr (-30% YoY); PAT (normalized): ₹10cr (ex-Teesa standalone profit of ₹3.37cr); Order Book: Not disclosed; Net Debt: ₹0.11x Net Debt/Equity (down from prior)
guidance: Revenue growth: 7-8% YoY; EBITDA margin: Targeting 7-8% by FY28; Order inflow: No explicit guidance; Capex/Commissioning: ₹55cr for backward dyeing unit (Dec’26/Jan’27); ₹8-9cr for renewable energy (Q1FY27)
segment / subsidiary detail: Core: Denim weaving (89.9% utilization); Forward integration: Teesta Spintex finishing unit (₹3.37cr PAT in H1, 30% job work); Backward integration: New dyeing unit (₹55cr capex, commissioning Dec’26/Jan’27); Renewable: 65% power from renewables, targeting 90% by FY27 with ₹8-9cr capex
growth verticals / optionality: Potential diversification into non-denim technical fabrics if denim demand softens; no B2C or brand launch planned; capacity expansion contingent on integration ROI
margins & cost dynamics: Current EBITDA margin 2.6% due to pricing compromise to maintain working capital; dyeing integration expected to add ₹12cr PAT; renewable energy to save ₹4.5-4.65cr annually (from ₹2.65cr today); cost advantage from 65% renewable power, zero debt, and wider looms (82-inch) lowers unit cost vs peers
capex / expansion: ₹55cr for backward dyeing unit (commissioning Dec’26/Jan’27); ₹8-9cr for renewable energy (Q1FY27); total capex ~₹63-64cr in next 12 months
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for vertical integration and renewable energy; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; net debt equity at 0.11x provides flexibility; excess cash deployed in bonds and AIF for other income
risks & watch-items: Pricing pressure from global tariffs and domestic competition; execution delay in dyeing unit commissioning; skill shortages during festive seasons; reliance on top 10 dealers for 99% revenue; no PLI benefits; margin expansion dependent on successful integration
management quality / tone: Confident and structured; focused on execution of integration roadmap; transparent on margin compression being temporary; emphasizes working capital discipline and zero debt as competitive advantages; avoids overpromising on volume growth
non-obvious takeaways: Teesta Spintex’s ₹3.37cr profit in H1 is largely from job work (30% of sales), not internal fabric conversion — meaning integration benefits are not yet fully captured in consolidated margins; the 82-inch loom advantage is a hidden differentiator in a market dominated by 210cm looms; AIF investment in equity markets adds non-operational income volatility
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shanti Spintex’s margin compression due to pricing compromise | Shanti Spintex Limited | beneficiary | High | Backward integration will eliminate ₹8-10/meter external dyeing costs, directly boosting PAT by ₹12cr |
| Competitors with higher debt and fossil-fuel power costs | Arvind Mills; Nandan Denim | loser | Medium | Shanti’s zero-debt and 65% renewable power create 15-20% cost advantage; peers lack similar vertical integration |
